Food boxes made from bamboo.

Factories in Huaihua, in China's Hunan province, are finding new uses for bamboo. Some pieces become chopsticks. Others are broken down into very small fibers. Workers use these fibers to make boxes for eggs, takeaway meals and other food.

The aim is to replace some plastic packaging with materials made from plants. One local company says its bamboo material is light and strong. Some of its products have passed tests showing that they can break down in home compost.

Bamboo grows quickly, and the mountains around Huaihua have large bamboo forests. People in the area have used the plant to make things for a very long time. Now factories are turning it into new everyday products. Food packaging is one way they hope to reduce plastic waste.
